'''Fr. Andrew Pinsent''' (born 1966) is professor of theology and philosophy at the [[Athenaeum of Ohio]]<ref>[https://www.athenaeum.edu/about/directory/father-andrew-pinsent/ "Athenaeum of Ohio, Faculty & Staff Directory>Father Andrew Pinsent]</ref> in Cincinnati, Ohio, and a Catholic priest of the [[Roman Catholic Diocese of Arundel and Brighton|Diocese of Arundel and Brighton]] in England. Until 2024, he was Research Director of the Ian Ramsey Centre for Science and Religion,<ref>[https://www.theology.ox.ac.uk/people/dr-andrew-pinsent "Dr Andrew Pinsent"], Faculty of Theology and Religion, University of Oxford.</ref> part of the Faculty of Theology and Religion at the [[University of Oxford]].<ref>[https://www.theology.ox.ac.uk/science-and-religion "Science and Religion"], Faculty of Theology and Religion, University of Oxford.</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ianramseycentre.info/personnel/dr-andrew-pinsent.html |title=Dr Andrew Pinsent - Research Director - Personnel |work=Ian Ramsey Centre |year=2015 |accessdate=16 August 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924032204/http://www.ianramseycentre.info/personnel/dr-andrew-pinsent.html |archive-date=24 September 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was also a Research Fellow at [[Harris Manchester College]], Oxford.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hmc.ox.ac.uk/people/fr-andrew-pinsent/ |title=Fr Andrew Pinsent |publisher =Harris Manchester College, University of Oxford}}</ref>

A physicist by training, Pinsent was involved in the [[DELPHI]] project at [[CERN]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://delphiwww.cern.ch/pubxx/delnote/dn_all.html|title=DELPHI Notes|work=CERN|accessdate=16 August 2015|archive-date=15 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150615183043/http://delphiwww.cern.ch/pubxx/delnote/dn_all.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> and co-authored 31 of the collaboration's publications. A focus of his current research is the application of insights from autism and social cognition to "second-person" accounts of moral perception and character formation.{{citation needed|date=August 2018}}

==Education and career==
Pinsent has a degree in physics and a D.Phil. in high-energy physics from [[Merton College]], Oxford. He also has three degrees in philosophy and theology from the [[Pontifical Gregorian University]] in Rome, and a Ph.D. in philosophy from [[Saint Louis University (United States)|Saint Louis University]].

A member of the United Kingdom [[Institute of Physics]] and a tutor of the Maryvale Institute in Birmingham, Pinsent has been interviewed for various media, including the [[BBC]]<ref>{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pBInzDv3zE0|title=BBC: The Big Questions: Is there evidence for God? |date=15 January 2012 |work=YouTube |accessdate=16 August 2015}}</ref> and [[EWTN]],<ref>{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qo78XSel0Eg |title=EWTN Live - Evangelium media course - Fr. Mitch Pacwa, SJ with Fr. Andrew Pinsent |date=28 July 2011 |work=YouTube |accessdate=16 August 2015}}</ref> on issues of science and faith. He has also written for the ''[[Catholic Herald]]'',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.catholicherald.co.uk/features/2011/05/06/what-the-church-has-given-the-world/|title=What the Church has given the world|work=Catholic Herald|accessdate=16 August 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923201130/http://www.catholicherald.co.uk/features/2011/05/06/what-the-church-has-given-the-world/|archive-date=23 September 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> who identified him as a prominent young Catholic.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.catholicherald.co.uk/features/2011/08/25/meet-ten-amazing-young-catholics/ |title=CatholicHerald.co.uk » Meet ten amazing young Catholics |first=Mary |last=O'Regan |work=Catholic Herald |date=25 August 2011 |accessdate=16 August 2015}}</ref> His most recent book is ''The Second-Person Perspective in Aquinas’s Ethics: Virtues and Gifts'' (2012). Besides academic publications, he is a co-author of the ''Evangelium'' catechetical course and the ''Credo'', ''Apologia,'' and ''Lumen'' pocket books.

In 2017, Pinsent signed a document along with a number of other clergy and academics labeled as a "[[Correctio filialis de haeresibus propagatis|Filial Correction]]" of Pope Francis.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.correctiofilialis.org/signatories/|title=Full list of the 250 signatories}}</ref>
